findings.text: Deliverable 4 (a skill section in `sub-mastermind`, plus a pointer in `mastermind`, saying when/how to run a collab) is missing entirely — the diff never touches any file under `.claude/skills/` or `.claude/agents/`. Nothing tells a mastermind this feature exists.

The Proof line asked for "one research run and one design run on real questions from today." Only the research run is real (`public/framework/ai/2026-09-28/collab-rounds/test-real/collab.jsonl`, real cost $0.32, real Servex agents). Every design run in the diff (`test-mock-design`, `test-mock-doclink`, `test-mock-target`) is `--mock`, cost $0, canned text — the staged names→vote→implement→cross-review→vote flow (deliverable 3) was never actually run against real agents.

Deliverable 5 asked for "a 3-member run in dollars." The only real, costed run has 2 members (`test-real`: haiku-a, haiku-b). The 3-member run that exists (`test-mock-research`, haiku-a/sonnet-b/haiku-c) is mock/$0, so the real per-member dollar cost at 3 members is still unproven.

The change goes well outside the stated fence (`ext/Collab/`, `Server/collab.mjs`, two skill sections): it adds `.claude/hooks/naming-guard.mjs` and wires it into `.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs:177`. This is a brand-new, always-on enforcement mechanism that fires on *every* `class` addition under `public/` in *every* future session, appending a nag line into that session's task.jsonl — a repo-wide behavior change requirements.md never asked for, on a shared hook file that isn't part of this task's fence. Per CLAUDE.md ("ask before... major surgery"), this needed a check-in first, not a silent ride-along on this task.

`ext/Doc/Doc.js:2830` and the new `ext/Doc/decisions.js` are also outside the fence, but this one is a reasonable, small, declared extension (wiring the ⋯ link to a named decision) rather than a global behavior change — noting it, not asking for a revert.

`Collab.js`'s `tallyVotes` (Server/collab.mjs:255) breaks a second-level tie by picking the *cheaper* member's proposal (`tie: cheaper member`), with no owner instruction backing "cheaper wins a tie" as a quality rule. In practice this will quietly favor Haiku over Sonnet whenever votes and caveats tie, which may not be the intended tie-break for a design vote. Worth a second look before this runs unattended.
